sections.skill: Follow approved tools, protect confidential information and review output at work

questions.prompt: Why might an employer allow some AI tools and not others?

choices.text: Because of how they handle data
Because some tools have nicer colors

questions.correct_answer: Because of how they handle data
questions.intro: Using AI responsibly at work starts with three habits. (1) Use APPROVED TOOLS: your employer may allow some tools and not others, often because of how they handle data. (2) Protect CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION: do not paste customer details, unreleased plans, passwords or private records into tools that are not approved for them. (3) REVIEW before output reaches others: check facts, tone and fit, because you are responsible for what you send. Also follow any rule about disclosing AI use, and ask your manager when the rules are unclear.

sections.skill: Compare AI rules at work with rules about company keys and badges

questions.prompt: Why does a badge open only some doors?

choices.text: The company decides what access is safe
Because badges are broken and should open every door in the building for every worker

questions.correct_answer: The company decides what access is safe
questions.intro: At many workplaces, your BADGE opens some doors but not others, and you would not lend it to a stranger or prop open a secure door because it is convenient. AI tools are similar: the company decides which tools you may use (which doors open), what information can go where (what you can carry out), and you remain responsible for what you do with your access.

sections.skill: Handle gray areas and mistakes at work

questions.prompt: You are unsure whether a document is confidential. What is the best approach?

choices.text: Assume it is public, since most workplace documents are not confidential anyway
Ask before using it in a tool

questions.correct_answer: Ask before using it in a tool
questions.intro: Gray areas are common. Is a customer's first name confidential? Can you summarize a public report with an unapproved tool? When unsure, ask before acting, and choose the more careful option. Watch for AI output that sounds right but conflicts with company policy, such as a promised refund the company does not offer. If you make a mistake, such as pasting private data into the wrong tool, report it promptly so it can be handled; hiding it makes it worse.
